uantwerp-summer-school-sustainable-city-.about:
The Sustainable City summer school (28 June – 2 July 2027) brings together city experts, practitioners and academics to look at how cities are changing to protect sustainable living conditions for all. Seminars and lectures by sociologists, planners, economists, historians and ecologists cover water and air quality, energy, circularity and biodiversity and how they interact with social inequality; participants visit innovative projects in Antwerp and finish with a group project on a real urban sustainability challenge.

It is aimed at master's students, PhD students and professionals in urban studies and related fields, who should hold a relevant bachelor's degree and show an interest in urban sustainability. Teaching is at the University of Antwerp's city-centre campus, and successful completion can earn ECTS credits.
highlights: Interdisciplinary view of urban sustainability
Site visits to sustainability projects in Antwerp
Group project on a real city challenge
uantwerp-summer-school-sustainable-city-.eligibility: Master's and PhD students and professionals in urban studies or related fields; a relevant academic bachelor's degree and demonstrated interest in urban sustainability; good English. All nationalities.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page
Apply on Mobility Online before 13 May 2027 (before 11 March if you need a visa)
Await selection
Pay the fee and arrange travel and accommodation
uantwerp-summer-school-sustainable-city-.costs: Tuition EUR 450 (EUR 300 for UAntwerp students), including course materials, welcome dinner, coffee breaks, lunches, an excursion and a farewell reception. Travel and accommodation not included.

uantwerp-summer-school-vaccinology-2027.about:
The Centre for the Evaluation of Vaccination at the University of Antwerp runs this annual summer school to fill a gap in many medical curricula. From 28 June to 5 July 2027, lecturers from across Europe teach vaccine-preventable infectious diseases, vaccine immunology, immunisation programmes, vaccine safety and how to communicate about vaccines, alongside practical training in administering vaccines. The week ends with a group task, and a social programme is organised by Antwerp medical students (EMSA).

It is designed for undergraduate and postgraduate (para-)medical students and PhD students, with a particular focus on the WHO European region, which includes Georgia. Places are capped at 50, with selection balanced by gender and nationality, and scholarships are available for undergraduate students from the WHO European region. Unusually, the fee includes accommodation and all meals on course days. ECTS credits can be awarded on completion.
highlights: Hands-on vaccine administration and communication training
Fee includes accommodation and meals
Scholarships for undergraduates from the WHO European region (incl. Georgia)
uantwerp-summer-school-vaccinology-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate, master's and PhD students in medicine and paramedical sciences (also residents and professionals at higher fees); focus on the WHO European region, which includes Georgia. Maximum 50 participants, balanced by gender and nationality.
how_to_apply: Read the programme and fee pages
Apply on Mobility Online before 27 March 2027
Indicate if you wish to be considered for a scholarship (WHO-Europe undergraduates)
If selected, pay the fee and arrange travel
uantwerp-summer-school-vaccinology-2027.costs: Tuition EUR 1,100 for students (and 2-year ESPID members), EUR 1,300 for postgraduate/PhD students and residents, EUR 2,500 for non-students; includes course material, accommodation, all meals on course days and social activities. Scholarships for WHO-Europe undergraduates. Travel not included.

uantwerp-winter-school-crisis-governance.about:
Part of the University of Antwerp's Antwerp Winter University, this intensive week (1–5 February 2027) explores how organisations anticipate, manage and learn from complex crises, from pandemics to operational disruptions. It combines crisis communication, decision-making under pressure, organisational resilience and network governance with guest lectures from crisis professionals, and participants work in groups on realistic crisis scenarios, presenting a governance strategy on the final day.

The school is designed for master's students and professionals working in, or aspiring to, crisis management roles, in public administration, emergency services, business or research. It takes place at the city-centre Stadscampus; successful completion (full participation and the group assignment) earns 3 ECTS credits and a micro-credential. Applications are reviewed by the academic committee.
highlights: Real crisis professionals as guest speakers
Hands-on crisis-scenario group work
3 ECTS micro-credential from the University of Antwerp
uantwerp-winter-school-crisis-governance.eligibility: Master's students and professionals (crisis management or aspiring); good English. Open to all nationalities; non-EU applicants arrange a Schengen visa (Georgian passport holders are visa-free for short stays).
how_to_apply: Read the programme and fee pages
Apply through the Mobility Online platform before 3 December 2026
Wait for selection by the academic committee
Pay the tuition fee to confirm your place
Book travel and accommodation in Antwerp
uantwerp-winter-school-crisis-governance.costs: Tuition EUR 450 for students, EUR 1,200 for professionals (EUR 300 for UAntwerp students). Includes course material, refreshments, lunch on Monday and Friday and excursion transport; travel and accommodation not included.

uantwerp-winter-school-european-solidari.about:
This third edition of the UCSIA winter school, 'Dignity Amidst Despair: Migration Challenging European Solidarity', runs from 1 to 5 February 2027 in Antwerp. Experts from philosophy, history, law and political science examine solidarity and human dignity, EU social rights and instruments for migrating workers, and the politics of EU migration and asylum policy. Participants travel to Brussels to meet policymakers, work with migrant-support organisations in Antwerp, and present their own findings at the end of the week.

It is designed for PhD candidates and final-year master's students from any discipline, and young professionals with a master's degree are also encouraged to apply; the organisers aim for an interdisciplinary, intercultural group. Good English is required. Successful completion can be recognised with 3 ECTS credits.
highlights: Field trip to EU institutions in Brussels
Meet migrant-support organisations in Antwerp
Low fee including lunches, excursion and farewell dinner
uantwerp-winter-school-european-solidari.eligibility: PhD candidates, final-year master's students and young professionals with a master's degree, any discipline and nationality; good command of English.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page
Apply on Mobility Online before 23 November 2026
Receive the selection outcome on 8 December 2026
Pay the fee and arrange visa, travel and accommodation
uantwerp-winter-school-european-solidari.costs: Tuition EUR 350 (EUR 200 for UAntwerp students), including course material, coffee breaks, lunches, social activities, an excursion and a farewell dinner. Travel and accommodation not included.

uantwerp-winter-school-global-food-law-p.about:
Run by the University of Antwerp's Faculty of Law with Roma Tre University, this course examines how law, policy and governance shape food production, circulation and consumption, and how they connect to food insecurity, health, climate change, labour and human rights. The first module is an academic week in Antwerp (1–5 February 2027); the second is a practitioner-based week in Rome (five days in late June/early July 2027, to be confirmed) with visits to the UN Rome-Based Agencies (FAO, IFAD, WFP), NGOs and EU representatives.

It is designed for undergraduates, master's students and PhD candidates interested in food law and policy, and for professionals from food-related sectors. Participants are expected to attend both modules; a limited number of hybrid places let students with limited means follow the Antwerp module online.
highlights: Two cities: Antwerp academic week and Rome practitioner week
Meetings with FAO, IFAD and WFP in Rome
Lower fees for Global South students and hybrid places
uantwerp-winter-school-global-food-law-p.eligibility: Undergraduate, master's and PhD students plus professionals with an interest in food systems; general familiarity with law or policy helpful; good English. All nationalities; Global South rate for students and professionals based there.
how_to_apply: Read the programme and fee pages
Apply via Mobility Online before 3 December 2026 (by 5 November if you need a visa)
Await selection by the academic committee
Pay the fee and plan travel to Antwerp and Rome
uantwerp-winter-school-global-food-law-p.costs: Tuition: EUR 900 for students at Global North universities, EUR 600 for students at Global South universities; professionals EUR 1,300 (Global North) or EUR 900 (Global South). Covers both modules, tutoring, workshops and receptions; travel, accommodation and most meals not included.

ucla-summer-college-immersion-program-20.about:
The UCLA Summer College Immersion Program (SCIP) gives academically advanced high-school students a six-week introduction to university life at UCLA. Participants enrol in approved UCLA undergraduate courses (earning UCLA credit) and attend co-curricular lectures, workshops and seminars on academic skills, research and the college application process, finishing with a certificate of completion. Variants include SCIP+ (research-skills focus) and eSCIP (online, from anywhere).

In 2026 the in-person SCIP ran 22 June – 31 July; UCLA's 2027 six-week Session A6 runs 21 June – 30 July 2027. International students who need a visa must apply earlier (1 April in 2026), enrol in two in-person SCIP courses to hold full-time F-1 status, and pay additional document fees. Admission is highly competitive.
highlights: Real UCLA credit courses with undergraduates
Workshops on college admissions, research and academic skills
Residential option in UCLA housing
ucla-summer-college-immersion-program-20.eligibility: High-school students in grades 10–11 (in spring of the programme year) with a minimum unweighted cumulative GPA of 3.8. International students are eligible; those needing an F-1 visa must take two in-person Session A6 SCIP-approved courses. All application materials must be in English.
how_to_apply: Watch summer.ucla.edu for the 2027 SCIP application (opened 18 February in 2026)
Submit the UCLA Summer Sessions application with full high-school transcript (with English translation) and a 350–500-word statement of purpose
International visa applicants: apply by about 1 April and pay the USD 350 registration fee by about 1 May
Enrol in courses on MyUCLA, request the I-20 and pay the balance by 1 June
ucla-summer-college-immersion-program-20.costs: 2026 fees: programme fee USD 1,675 + per-unit fees (about USD 385/unit) + USD 350 registration fee + USD 50 document fee for visa students; housing extra. Use UCLA's fee calculator for totals.

ugr-clm-granada-summer-spanish-language-.about:
The Centro de Lenguas Modernas (CLM) is the University of Granada's own language centre, accredited by the Instituto Cervantes. Its 'Curso de verano de Lengua y Cultura' runs in two monthly sessions in 2027, 2–29 June and 2–29 July (or both, 180 hours). Each month students build a 90-hour timetable from Spanish language classes and 22.5- or 45-hour subjects such as Spanish and Latin American literature, history of Spain and its art, Islamic culture in Spain, Spanish business law, international marketing, renewable energy and sustainability in the Mediterranean; a few June subjects are taught in English, and internships (volunteering, law, business, healthcare) can be added.

The course is for intermediate and advanced learners (B1.1 to C2) and suits university students who want transferable credit and a summer in Granada, home of the Alhambra. The CLM also offers accommodation help, cultural and sports activities and a language exchange.
highlights: University of Granada language centre, Instituto Cervantes accredited
90 hours per month: Spanish plus culture, literature and business subjects
June and/or July 2027 in Granada
ugr-clm-granada-summer-spanish-language-.eligibility: Learners of Spanish at level B1.1 or above (up to C2), normally aged 18+; all nationalities. Non-EU citizens arrange their own Schengen visa if needed (Georgian citizens travel visa-free for stays under 90 days).
how_to_apply: Choose June, July or both on the 2027 course page
Select subjects adding up to 90 hours per month
Register online through the CLM 'Inscripción' link and pay the first instalment
Take the level test at the start of the course
Book accommodation through the CLM or independently
ugr-clm-granada-summer-spanish-language-.costs: 2027 fee: EUR 1,395 per month (first instalment EUR 558) or EUR 2,664 for June + July (first instalment EUR 1,066). Accommodation, travel and insurance not included.

uli-hines-student-competition-asia-pacif.about:
The ULI Hines Student Competition Asia Pacific, in its fifth year in 2027, asks multidisciplinary teams of graduate and final-year undergraduate students to develop a creative, sustainable and commercially viable proposal for a real site in a major Asia Pacific city, reimagining it as a vibrant mixed-use, transit-oriented neighbourhood.

Teams register by 3 March 2027; the brief and site are released on 9 March and teams have until 30 March to submit. Finalists are announced on 31 March and present virtually on 16 April 2027. Since 2023 it has drawn 580+ students from 36 universities in Australia, China, India, Hong Kong, Japan, Pakistan, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam.

All finalists receive a one-year ULI student membership and networking with industry leaders; the winning team gets a fully paid trip (flights, hotel, delegate pass) to the ULI Asia Pacific Summit 2027 (26–28 May) and mentorship from Hines leaders.
highlights: Real site, real industry judges
Winners flown to the ULI Asia Pacific Summit 2027
Great for architecture, planning, real estate and finance students
uli-hines-student-competition-asia-pacif.eligibility: Graduate and final-year undergraduate students at universities in the Asia Pacific region, in multidisciplinary teams (e.g. architecture, planning, real estate, finance, engineering). Check the official terms for team size and eligible universities.
how_to_apply: Form a multidisciplinary team with a faculty adviser.
Team leader creates a ULI account and registers the team by 3 March 2027, 11:59pm HKT.
Receive the brief on 9 March and submit your proposal by 30 March 2027.
Finalists present online on 16 April 2027.
uli-hines-student-competition-asia-pacif.costs: Free to enter. Winning team trip fully paid (flights, accommodation, summit pass).

wake-forest-summer-immersion-2027.about:
Wake Forest University's Summer Immersion Program offers week-long, career-focused institutes on its campus in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. STEM options include Artificial Intelligence, Biology Research, Coding and Computer Science, Engineering, Health and Exercise Science, Medicine, Neuroscience, Psychology, Regenerative Medicine, Sports Medicine, Technology and Women's Health; other institutes cover business, finance, entrepreneurship, law, policy, debate, filmmaking and writing. Students attend all five days, live in a supervised residence hall and earn a certificate.

The 2027 application opens on 1 November 2026 and admission is rolling until institutes are full, so applying early matters. International students are encouraged to apply and do not need a TOEFL score, but they cannot receive the need-based scholarships. 2027 week dates are published on the programme's Dates page.
highlights: Wide choice of one-week STEM and career institutes
Residential college experience with 24/7 supervision
Rolling admission from 1 November; no TOEFL required
wake-forest-summer-immersion-2027.eligibility: Current 9th–12th grade students in good academic standing with no school suspensions; home-schooled students welcome. International students are encouraged to apply (no TOEFL needed) but are not eligible for need-based aid.
how_to_apply: Apply online from 1 November 2026 and pay the USD 65 application fee
Show interest in one or more institutes; admission is rolling
Once admitted, choose a week and pay the USD 550 non-refundable deposit to secure a seat
Pay the remaining tuition by 2 April 2027 (or in full on registration after that date)
wake-forest-summer-immersion-2027.costs: USD 3,500 per institute (2026 rate; subject to change), USD 65 application fee, USD 550 deposit counted toward tuition. Travel to the US not included. Need-based scholarships for domestic students only.

waseda-summer-session-2027.about:
The Waseda Summer Session is run by Waseda University's Global Immersion Programs in central Tokyo. In 2026 it ran from 15 June to 22 July, with English-taught courses on Japanese society, culture, business and Asia, alongside cultural activities, field trips and Waseda student interns.

It is open to university students from around the world with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5/4.0; students from non-English-medium universities are recommended to have TOEFL iBT 79 or IELTS 6.0.

The 2027 session is expected to open for applications in February 2027 with a deadline at the end of that month; fees and accommodation options are published on the programme pages.
highlights: Study at one of Japan's top private universities
English-taught courses on Japan and Asia
Cultural activities with Waseda student interns
waseda-summer-session-2027.eligibility: University students worldwide with cumulative GPA 2.5/4.0+; recommended TOEFL iBT 79 / IELTS 6.0 for non-English-medium students.
how_to_apply: Check the Summer Session pages (dates, courses, tuition, accommodation) for 2027.
Apply online when applications open (February).
Submit transcript and English proof as requested.
Pay tuition and arrange accommodation after admission.
waseda-summer-session-2027.costs: Tuition and accommodation fees are listed on the official Tuition and Fees page; travel and living costs extra.

world-masters-games-2027-kansai-voluntee.about:
The World Masters Games are the world's largest multi-sport event for adult athletes (roughly 30 and over). The 2027 edition is hosted across the Kansai region of Japan (Osaka, Kyoto, Hyogo, Shiga, Nara, Wakayama and more), opening on 14 May 2027.

Volunteers support venues, athlete services and visitors in a chosen prefecture or city. You pick a location and activity from the volunteer page and apply through that local committee; each committee sets its own details and deadlines.

Volunteers must be 18 or older on 1 April 2027, speak everyday conversational Japanese, attend common and role-specific training, work 5–8 hours a day and arrange their own lodging and transport. It suits international students already living in Japan; a uniform is provided and can be kept afterwards.
highlights: Be part of a major international sports event in Japan
Uniform provided (yours to keep)
Choose your city and role across Kansai
world-masters-games-2027-kansai-voluntee.eligibility: Aged 18+ as of 1 April 2027; everyday conversational Japanese; able to attend training and work 5–8 hours a day. Nationality not restricted, but lodging and transport are self-arranged, so best for residents of Japan.
how_to_apply: Open the volunteer page on wmg2027.jp.
Choose a prefecture or city and activity from the banners.
Apply through that local committee's application page before its deadline.
Attend the common and role-specific training sessions.
world-masters-games-2027-kansai-voluntee.costs: Free to volunteer. Uniform provided. Lodging and transport are at your own cost.
